acceptance.statement: Default product path discovers tenant-scoped Agora DatasetVersions regardless of policy-store backend.
Dataset lookup failure is degraded and never substitutes seed data.
Scheduler and worker use claim lease and survive duplicate ticks and restart.
Authoritative training evaluation and candidate artifacts retain dataset lineage.
Candidate cannot affect runtime before experiment approval and deployment gates.
Direct tick, claim, replay, and readback routes are trusted and tenant-bound.

proof: Candidate identity is a digest of (tenant, tick, dataset version), so a duplicate tick, a scheduler restart inside the same window, and two schedulers racing all resolve to the same candidate id instead of minting colliding backlog-length counters.

Creation is insert-if-absent: Postgres uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING against a UNIQUE (dedupe_key) index and JSON performs the check and the insert inside one flock-held read-modify-write, so six concurrent ticks of the same tick_id produce each candidate exactly once.

A dataset-authority failure produces a degraded candidate carrying an explicit seed_fallback_used: false and authoritative: false; no branch of the product path returns seed, fixture, or synthesized data.

A damaged JSON backlog raises CandidateStoreCorrupt and every affected route answers HTTP 503 CANDIDATE_STORE_CORRUPT, so a corrupt backlog can never present as an idle healthy loop, and a tick will not overwrite it.
Every processed candidate retains the Agora dataset lineage on the candidate row, the trained artifact, and the training evaluation, including dataset_version_ids, content_sha256, and payload_sha256.
The scheduler sidecar presents its service token and X-Tenant-Id, and the tick response echoes the authenticated actor and tenant it scheduled under.

Real two-process proof against real PostgreSQL: a worker claims the backlog under a short lease, is SIGKILLed with no settle and no lease release, the survivor takes nothing while the lease is live, and after expiry release_expired_leases returns exactly the dead worker's candidates for reclaim at attempt_count 2.
A brand new store handle standing in for a restarted container reads back the same authoritative rows, and a fresh empty data directory still sees the Postgres-backed backlog.
settle_candidate compares the presented lease token under FOR UPDATE (or the file lock) and raises LeaseLostError, so a revived worker cannot overwrite the new owner's result.

requeue_candidate refuses (HTTP 409 CANDIDATE_LEASE_HELD) while a live lease exists, so retry and DLQ replay cannot create a second run that also believes it is authoritative; replay of a degraded candidate reruns it cleanly once the authority returns.

json_backlog_remains_reachable_without_a.containment: Only reachable when no POLICY_LEARNING_STORE_DSN and no DATABASE_URL is configured, or when POLICY_LEARNING_CANDIDATE_AUTHORITY=json is set explicitly. The resolution is reported on /health and /readyz as durable: false with its reason, and the JSON path is still lease-fenced, atomically written, and fail-closed on corruption.
json_backlog_remains_reachable_without_a.description: A deployment with no database configured at all keeps a non-durable JSON candidate backlog. It is labelled rather than refused, so an operator who removes the DSN loses durability without the loop refusing to run.
json_backlog_remains_reachable_without_a.recheck_trigger: Any change to policy-learning persistence posture enforcement, or a decision to make a missing DSN fail closed in the product path.

shared_dsn_read_role_not_yet_separated.containment: The cross-owner Agora session is pinned read_only, so policy-learning physically cannot write agora.* even when it falls back to the shared DATABASE_URL, and an anonymous connection is refused. describe() reports dedicated_read_role_dsn so an operator can see whether a separate role is in use.
shared_dsn_read_role_not_yet_separated.description: Compose gives policy-learning only DATABASE_URL, so unless AGORA_DATASET_STORE_DSN names a dedicated read role the Agora read reuses the shared application role. Provisioning that role is a deployment-configuration change and is out of this task's no-config-change boundary.
shared_dsn_read_role_not_yet_separated.recheck_trigger: The next change to Pantheon Postgres role provisioning or to DATABASE_OWNERSHIP_AND_SHARED_CLUSTER_POLICY.md read-role enforcement.

composes_with: L12-AGORA-001 governed Agora dataset extraction owner
scope.not_changing: docker-compose files, env templates, or any other configuration; live Pantheon service, database, or runtime state; registry artifacts, deployment stages, RuntimeBinding, capital binding, or order routing; the pre-existing policy-learning job and capability route surface.
scope.owned_layer: Authenticated tenant-bound direct tick/claim/process/restart/retry/replay/candidate/readback routes, atomic (tenant, tick, dataset version) candidate authority with collision-free ids, lease fencing at settle and requeue, durable Postgres candidate authority in the product path, authenticated read-only cross-owner Agora resolution with no seed fallback, fail-closed backlog corruption handling, and the proof suite for all of it

environment_boundary.proof: Verification used a localhost-only throwaway postgres:16-alpine container and in-process ASGI clients. No compose file, env template, live service, or live database was modified.

mfa.proof: No route in this surface performs an irreversible operator action; the loop produces research candidates that are fail-closed against promotion.

no_live_capital.proof: policy-learning imports no registry, deployment, RuntimeBinding, capital, broker, or order-routing writer. promote always answers 409 and mutates nothing, and the governance report enumerates those authorities as denied.

rbac.proof: Every direct imitation-loop route requires a verified caller holding a configured role; a verified JWT with the wrong role is 403 and one with no role claim at all fails closed instead of defaulting to operator.

tenant_isolation.proof: The tenant comes from the verified request, not the body. A body tenant that disagrees is 403 TENANT_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH, a dataset_ref naming another tenant is rejected rather than re-stamped, cross-tenant candidate reads answer 404 so ids cannot be enumerated, claims are tenant-filtered, and concurrent cross-tenant ticks and claims were proven disjoint in threads and against real PostgreSQL row locks.

two_person_approval.proof: Owner Claude and reviewer Codex2 are distinct. Independent review of the exact final head is pending and is recorded in record_log when it happens.
